What a multi-eventer Maureen Knight could be. This time she went on a points scoring spree and ended up with four first places and a second.
Maureen Knight made her first appearance in the team for the Salisbury match and immediately picked up a win in the high jump and gained further good points in the long jump and javelin.

Three first places went to Maureen Knight and the points were piling up but, missing a few specialist middle-distance runners, in the end it was the Essex club that just prevailed while the Belles kept just 4 points clear of the home club Blackheath.

As we put together this magazine and type up the results we cannot help but be impressed by the huge contribution made towards our points scores by Maureen Knight.

Maureen Knight placed second in the javelin where she deputised for Goldie Sayers, on Under-23 international duty in Poland Chris Moss back on the track after his knee injury was always in control of the 800 metres.
Michelle Nestor squeezed a fifth spot in a closely contested long jump while Maureen Knight occupied the same spot in the high jump as she embarked on a busy afternoon schedule.

Maureen Knight, 'fresh' from gaining a silver medal in the British Isles Combined Events Cup, won the high jump A, the javelin B and was only a fraction below her season's best of 11.47 in a high calibre triple jump competition where the first four achieved grade 2 jumps.
She also won the 800m B and javelin B (26.81), where Maureen Knight came second in the A competition with 35.75 metres to contribute to her afternoon of points collection.
